newsitem.title: USA: Banks agree to $155 mln for U.S. football stadium.
newsitem.headline: Banks agree to $155 mln for U.S. football stadium.

text.p: The Washington Redskins said on Wednesday that the team has reached a final agreement with a consortium of banks for $155 million in financing for its new 78,600-seat football stadium in Prince Georges County, Maryland.

The consortium, headed by Sumitomo Bank Ltd and NationsBank Corp, also includes Fleet National Bank and First Union National Bank as co-agents and Provident Bank and Chevy Chase Bank as lenders, the Redskins said in a statement.

The luxury facility on 200 acres has a total estimated price tag of $180 million. The Redskins said it will be completed in a record 17.5 months, in time for a September 14, 1997, opening game with the Arizona Cardinals.

The state of Maryland and Prince Georges County, Maryland, have kicked in an additional $70.5 million in transportation infrastructure improvements for the privately financed stadium, including widening roads and constructing new overpasses and a new interchange on the Washington Beltway.
